written_before: any v3 model was trained for real, exported or scored (only a 3-step plumbing smoke run of the training and export code existed); the value labels were already built, with no v3 score available
question: gidi-en has no value (amount) span. Does v2 + a learned value-span head (the value-span-v1 head design) reach the declared value quality without regressing type or target?
label_provenance: silver-claude-clef-regex; no human labels exist for English. Value labels = labeler A (deterministic en-US/UK/IN/SG amount scan, src/gidi/value_parser/english.py) + labeler B (Clef zero-shot choice among A's loose candidates, experiments/gidi-en-student-v3/run_value_teacher.py) -> consensus where they agree, Claude adjudicates only the disagreements (datasets/annotation-en-v1/work/value/adjudicated.jsonl). Files: datasets/annotation-en-v1/value-labels-{test,dev,seed,probe-slang,probe-genz}.jsonl, value-silver-train.jsonl, value-silver-slang-train.jsonl. Never human. All numbers are agreement with these labels, not ground truth.
value_contract: configs/annotation-en-v1.yaml `value:` + docs/annotation-en-v1.md 'Amount formats': the amount exactly as written (currency symbol, prefix code or money word included: `$20`, `20 bucks`, `s$30`, `150s$`, `rs 500`, `3 grand`), no normalisation, null when the note has no amount, `uncertain` when no transaction amount can be told apart (masked in the value loss). Word amounts are spans too (`twenty bucks`, `a hundred`, `tenner`, `fiver`; the article of `a tenner` is not part of it, the article of `a hundred` is). `4` / `2` standing for `for` / `to` are not amounts. Clarified in docs/annotation-en-v1.md before training.
candidate: v3 seed 1 only (one seed, last epoch, no seed picking, no checkpoint selection).
recipe: v2 recipe unchanged (experiments/gidi-en-student-v2/run.sh): init models/gidi-en-v1-init, silver-train + labels-seed + consistent silver-slang-train = 2,355 notes, 40 epochs, batch 8, encoder lr 5e-5, head lr 1e-3, warmup 0.1, wd 0.01, grad clip 1.0, shuffles randperm(seed + epoch), MPS, same code path (scripts/train_en_student.py --value). The only change is the added head and its loss.
head: Value-span-v1 design (gidi.modeling.value.GidiValueModel, the shared-encoder 3-head model of experiments/value-span-v1): Linear(hidden=768, 3) over the same dropout-ed token states as the target head, tags O/B-VALUE/I-VALUE, seeded from VALUE_HEAD_SEED_BASE + seed with the global RNG untouched (so the encoder init and the dropout / shuffle streams match v2). Not the CRF / MLP / adapter / dual-encoder variants of value-span-v4..v7 (they do not fit the ~30 MB budget or were frozen-encoder experiments); gidi-finance-v4 itself ships no learned value head (rule parser, `value_source: rule-parser`), the learned head lineage is value-span-v1 -> gidi-finance-v2.
loss: CE(type) + CE(target tags) + CE(value tags), equal weights (gidi.training.train_value.multitask_loss). Value tags of any note whose value_status is not `complete` are IGNORE_INDEX (such a note still trains type and target); a `complete` note with value null has every real token O.
decode: Value = the highest-confidence BIO span of the value head (gidi.modeling.value_decode.decode_value, value-span-v1), argmax per token. Target = first span, as v2.
snapping: decision: value spans are scored with whole-word snapping ON (gidi.inference.decode.snap_to_words, the rule v2 applies to the target), because it only expands a truncated span to whole words and a check on all 3,160 gold value spans found it changes 2 (`300` -> `+300`, a leading sign), i.e. it is consistent with the label convention. Unsnapped scores are reported as an ablation. It is not in the ONNX graph (same as the target).
export: ONNX opset 17 via scripts/export_value_onnx.py: outputs type_logits, tag_logits, value_logits (names/order of the Vietnamese value bundle), int8 = dynamic QInt8 as v2. Op set must equal v2's.
training_data: silver-train + labels-seed complete + silver-slang-train (consistent only), with their silver value labels. Never: test, dev, datasets/probe-en-slang, datasets/probe-en-genz, Vietnamese data (asserted in gidi.training.english.load_train_values_v2).

eval_sets.test_primary: complete test notes with consensus type/target labels (n = 214)
eval_sets.genz_probe: datasets/probe-en-genz complete notes (n = 94), reported, not gating
eval_sets.dev: complete dev notes (n = 189), reported, not gating (monitored during training)

value_exact_min.note: value exact = predicted span equals the labelled span, null equals null, over the notes whose value label is complete; test threshold applies to BOTH test primary and test secondary; slang probe n = 357; snapped decode

success.regression_note: type macro-F1 and target exact of v3 must each be >= v2 - 0.01 on test primary, test secondary and the slang probe (v2 snapped int8 numbers above)
success.beats_scanner: value exact of v3 >= value exact of the playground scanner `findEnglishValue` (playground/src/app/amount.ts, run via experiments/gidi-en-student-v3/app_scanner.ts) on test primary, test secondary and the slang probe. Gating on `core_exact` (currency symbols and money words stripped from both spans, because the scanner by design returns the number without them while the annotation convention keeps them); `exact` (strict, span equal to the gold span) is reported next to it. Both are reported for every set.
success.rule: all conditions must hold; PASS or FAIL is reported as is. No threshold, data, seed, decode or label change after seeing any v3 score.

circularity_caveat: Labeler A (regex scan) and the playground scanner are both deterministic rule scans for the same amount shapes, and notes where A and Clef agree (97.5%) were never reviewed by a human or by Claude, so the labels favour rule-like behaviour and the scanner comparison is optimistic for the scanner on consensus notes. Reported per set and for the adjudicated subset.
